name: Voriconazole
route_note: IV infusion or oral tablets/suspension twice daily after a loading dose; therapeutic drug monitoring often used

discovery.note: Fluconazole derivative with a fluoropyrimidine ring that extends the spectrum to Aspergillus and other moulds.

tagline: First-line drug for invasive aspergillosis, with notable visual and skin side effects
summary: Voriconazole is a second-generation triazole derived from fluconazole with activity against Aspergillus, Fusarium, Scedosporium and resistant Candida. It became the standard first-line treatment for invasive aspergillosis after it outperformed amphotericin B in a landmark 2002 trial. Its nonlinear pharmacokinetics and CYP2C19 polymorphisms make blood-level monitoring important.
mechanism: Azoles inhibit lanosterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51, encoded by ERG11 in yeasts and cyp51A in Aspergillus), a fungal cytochrome P450 enzyme needed to make ergosterol, the main sterol of fungal cell membranes. Ergosterol depletion and accumulation of toxic 14α-methylated sterols disrupt membrane structure and the function of membrane-bound enzymes, stopping fungal growth.

Voriconazole is fungicidal against Aspergillus species but generally fungistatic against Candida. It has no meaningful activity against the Mucorales, and breakthrough mucormycosis has been reported during voriconazole prophylaxis.
uses: Candidaemia in non-neutropenic patients and other deep Candida infections
Serious infections caused by Scedosporium and Fusarium species
Prophylaxis in high-risk haematopoietic stem-cell transplant recipients (EU)

history.title: Landmark trial
history.detail: Herbrecht and colleagues report better response and survival with voriconazole than conventional amphotericin B for invasive aspergillosis (NEJM).

history.title: Approval
history.detail: Vfend is approved by the EU in March and the FDA in May 2002.

history.title: Guidelines
history.detail: IDSA aspergillosis guidelines recommend voriconazole as primary therapy.

history.title: Skin cancer signal
history.detail: Reports link long-term voriconazole with phototoxicity and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, especially in transplant recipients.

history.title: WHO essential medicine
history.detail: Voriconazole is added to the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines.

pk.half_life: dose-dependent, about 6 h at standard doses (nonlinear)
pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP2C19 (main), CYP2C9 and CYP3A4; inhibits these enzymes

common: transient visual disturbances (blurred vision, altered colour perception, photophobia)
serious: QT prolongation and torsades de pointes
cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma and melanoma with long-term use
periostitis and fluorosis with prolonged use

facts: About 30% of patients notice transient visual changes, typically shortly after a dose.
Each voriconazole molecule contains three fluorine atoms; prolonged use can cause fluoride excess and painful periostitis.
IV voriconazole contains a cyclodextrin that can accumulate in renal failure.

references.title: Herbrecht R et al. Voriconazole versus amphotericin B for primary therapy of invasive aspergillosis. NEJM 2002
